newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt drifts in a range, awaits new impulses.
newsitem.headline: German debt drifts in a range, awaits new impulses.

text.p: German debt drifted sideways on Friday, lacking the necessary momentum to move either higher or lower and saving its energy for next week, dealers said.
By 1549 GMT the March DTB Bund futures contract was trading down 11 basis points at 103.35, having traded between 103.43 and 103.18 during the session.
At the same time the benchmark cash bond was at 103.44 compared with Thursday's 103.51 level.
Dealers said the market lacked direction even though U.S. Treasury prices opened mostly higher today as investors were taking advantage of lower prices.
After stronger than expected German economic data on Thursday, dealers said the market's rally may have come to a temporary end, suggesting a deeper correction would be likely next week.
Some saw the futures moving to 102.75 next week, but since support held well today, others said a downward correction may be some time away.
As long as the 103 level holds, dealers said the market could still generate new momentum and test higher next week.
